references.text: Also in Mark, evil spirits are driven out, and they cry out Jesus' identity. Jesus commands them to be silent, as in Luke 4:41.
Mark's parallel text to Luke 4:41 – Jesus heals many sick people and drives out evil spirits, but does not allow them to speak because they knew him.
The unclean spirits fell down before Jesus and cried out, "You are the Son of God!", and Jesus strictly forbade them from making him known – the same pattern as in Luke 4:41.
The demons recognize Jesus as the Son of God and cry it out, showing that evil spirits knew who Jesus was, just as in Luke 4:41.
Jesus heals many, but commands them not to make him known. This reflects Jesus' desire to keep his messianic identity hidden, as in Luke 4:41.
Earlier in the same chapter, an unclean spirit recognizes Jesus as "the Holy One of God" and Jesus silences it – a direct parallel motif to verse 41.
A spirit cries out the truth about Paul and his companions, but Paul commands the spirit to come out – a similar pattern where evil spirits testify truly but are rejected.
Even the evil spirits believe that God is one, and they shudder. This confirms that demons have knowledge of God's identity, just as the demons in Luke 4:41 knew that Jesus was the Christ.
The possessed man in Gerasa cries out that Jesus is "the Son of the Most High God" – the demons recognize Jesus' divine identity, as in Luke 4:41.
Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God, but Jesus commands the disciples not to tell anyone further. The messianic secret is a central theme also seen in Luke 4:41.
Peter confesses Jesus as "the Holy One of God" – the true confession of Jesus' identity that even the demons in Luke 4:41 knew.
